own.claim: Do not chase a document you have sent until at least a week has passed and the recipient's normal response window has closed.
own.why: A chase before the recipient has had time to review reads as pressure and damages the relationship; it also violates the rule against chasing while the ball is in their court.

own.claim: Integration discussions with potential partners often move slowly because they require internal review, legal clearance, or technical evaluation.
own.why: The counterparty may be waiting for internal stakeholders to weigh in before responding.

own.claim: A file with no playbook and no role in the brief should not be carried as an active item; it should be closed or reclassified.
own.why: Carrying items with no defined work type inflates the ledger and obscures genuine commitments.

patterns.claim: Integration documents sent to potential partners typically receive acknowledgment or feedback within three to five business days.
Silence after sending a requested document does not indicate rejection; it often indicates the recipient is reviewing it or has deprioritized it.
A file with no extracted promise and no named kind of work in the brief is often a transactional exchange rather than a tracked commitment.
